description: Goat hide, marketed as morocco, prized as a covering skin for fine work because of its firm grain and toughness. It appears under several regional trade names, and Cockerell singles out a West African goatskin as the most durable he had used while noting it often arrives flawed and unevenly prepared.
name: goatskin

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
